security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of malware, prompt injection, unauthorized data exfiltration, or hidden execution intent. The flagged patterns are CI/CD examples involving shell commands, public service URLs, secret references, and local file paths in documentation. These examples are legitimate for the skill, but authors should add stronger guardrails for secrets, deployment approvals, and plan-output disclosure.

remediation.issue: Cloud deployment examples use long-lived AWS credential secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer GitHub OIDC federation with short-lived roles, least privilege, and protected production environments.

remediation.issue: Terraform plan output is posted to pull request comments.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize plan summaries and restrict comments to trusted pull requests or internal branches.

remediation.issue: Setup examples install global tools and start local containers.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review scripts first, pin tool versions, and run setup only in trusted project directories.

remediation.issue: Several third-party actions and tools are referenced by version tags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin high-risk actions to trusted versions or commit SHAs and document update ownership.

content.value_statement: Manual release work creates delays, missed checks, and inconsistent deployments. This skill helps plan CI/CD workflows with tests, approvals, secrets handling, and rollback notes.
actual_capabilities: Maps build, test, release, and deployment stages from project context.
Suggests GitHub Actions and multi-stage workflow patterns.
Identifies required secrets, environment variables, and service integrations.
Adds quality gates, security scans, approvals, and notifications.
Documents rollout, rollback, risks, and operational assumptions.
limitations: Does not execute deployments or verify cloud permissions by itself.
Requires current project scripts, environments, and release policies.
Generated workflow files need review before production use.
Provider-specific syntax may need adjustment for each repository.

use_cases.title: Create a First CI Pipeline
use_cases.description: Turn existing build and test commands into a repeatable workflow with clear triggers and checks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Automation
use_cases.description: Define release, changelog, artifact, and notification steps for consistent delivery across services.

use_cases.title: Improve Deployment Governance
use_cases.description: Add approvals, environment gates, rollback notes, and security scans to deployment workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CI workflow for this project. Include install, lint, test, build, caching, and clear trigger recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Add Release Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a release workflow that creates artifacts, release notes, version tags, and notifications. List required secrets and approvals.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Deployment Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this deployment process and add quality gates, secret handling, rollback steps, smoke tests, and production approvals.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Environment Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multi-environment CI/CD system for development, staging, and production. Include promotion rules, artifacts, observability, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: A Node.js service needs CI for pull requests and main branch builds.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow plan with dependency caching, linting, tests, build artifacts, branch triggers, and required repository settings.

output_examples.input: A team wants safer production deployments from GitHub Actions.
output_examples.output: A deployment plan with environment approvals, least-privilege secrets, smoke tests, notifications, and rollback checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A repository has manual release notes and package publishing.
output_examples.output: A release automation outline covering versioning, changelog generation, package publishing, artifact retention, and stakeholder alerts.

best_practices: Review generated workflows before enabling production triggers.
Use least-privilege secrets, environment approvals, and auditable deployment gates.
Test pipeline changes on non-production branches before broad rollout.
anti_patterns: Running deployment jobs without approvals, rollback steps, or environment protection.
Copying workflow examples without adapting secrets, permissions, and branch rules.
Treating successful builds as production readiness without tests or verification.

faq.question: Can this skill write GitHub Actions workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose workflow files, stages, triggers, secrets, and review notes for GitHub Actions.

faq.question: Does it run deployment commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides plans and workflow suggestions. Users must approve and run deployments in their own systems.

faq.question: Can it support tools besides GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance can be adapted for GitLab CI, Jenkins, Terraform, Helm, Docker, and release tools.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use platform secret stores, least privilege, environment protections, and short-lived credentials where available.

faq.question: Is the generated workflow production ready?
faq.answer: It is a starting point. Review permissions, deployment gates, provider syntax, and rollback behavior before production use.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing pipeline?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current process and goals, and it can suggest caching, quality gates, security scans, and release improvements.
